content.text:
Below is a **classic first-time China itinerary** that fits well into 7 days: **Beijing → Xi’an → Shanghai**. It gives you imperial history, the Great Wall, Terracotta Warriors, food markets, and modern China without moving too fast.

## Quick notes before booking

- If you’re a U.S. passport holder, check your visa situation. China’s **240-hour visa-free transit** can apply to eligible travelers, including U.S. citizens, if you’re transiting through China to a **third country/region** and meet the routing rules; otherwise, you may need a tourist visa. Confirm before booking flights. ([english.www.gov.cn](https://english.www.gov.cn/english.www.gov.cn/news/202412/17/content_WS6760ead6c6d0868f4e8ee0c1.html?utm_source=openai))  
- Best seasons: **April–May** and **September–October** for comfortable weather.
- Use **high-speed trains** where possible; they’re efficient and part of the experience.
- Install before arrival: **Alipay or WeChat Pay**, a translation app, and a map app that works in China.

---

# 7-Day China Itinerary: Beijing, Xi’an & Shanghai

## Day 1 — Arrive in Beijing: Hutongs + Peking Duck

**Arrive:** Beijing Capital Airport or Daxing Airport  
**Stay:** Dongcheng, Wangfujing, Qianmen, or Sanlitun

**Plan**
- Check in and take it easy after the flight.
- Walk through **Qianmen Street** or the **hutongs** around Shichahai/Nanluoguxiang.
- Dinner: **Peking duck**.

**Good evening options**
- Casual: hutong food walk
- Classic: Da Dong, Siji Minfu, or Quanjude-style roast duck
- Low-key: stroll around Houhai Lake

---

## Day 2 — Beijing: Forbidden City, Tiananmen, Temple of Heaven

**Morning**
- Visit **Tiananmen Square** and the **Forbidden City**.
- Book Forbidden City tickets in advance if possible.

**Afternoon**
- Go to **Jingshan Park** for the best panoramic view over the Forbidden City.
- Visit the **Temple of Heaven**, one of Beijing’s most atmospheric imperial sites.

**Evening**
- Explore **Wangfujing** or Sanlitun.
- Try: zhajiangmian, dumplings, lamb skewers, jianbing, hotpot.

**Tip:** This is a heavy walking day. Wear comfortable shoes.

---

## Day 3 — Great Wall Day Trip + Summer Palace or Olympic Park

**Morning to afternoon**
- Visit the **Great Wall**.  
  Best sections:
  - **Mutianyu** — best for most first-timers; scenic and less chaotic than Badaling.
  - **Badaling** — easier transport, more crowded, officially promoted as a major Beijing attraction. ([english.beijing.gov.cn](https://english.beijing.gov.cn/travellinginbeijing/attractions/?utm_source=openai))  
  - **Jinshanling** — better for hikers and photographers, farther out.

**Late afternoon**
- If energy allows, visit the **Summer Palace**.

**Evening**
- Relax with dinner near your hotel.
- Optional: see the Bird’s Nest and Water Cube lit up at Olympic Park.

---

## Day 4 — Beijing → Xi’an: City Wall + Muslim Quarter

**Travel**
- Take a high-speed train from **Beijing West to Xi’an North**.
- Journey time is usually around 4.5–6 hours depending on train.

**Afternoon**
- Check in near the Bell Tower, South Gate, or Giant Wild Goose Pagoda area.
- Walk or cycle the **Xi’an City Wall**.

**Evening**
- Visit the **Muslim Quarter** for street food.
- Try: roujiamo, biangbiang noodles, lamb skewers, persimmon cakes, dumplings in sour soup.

---

## Day 5 — Xi’an: Terracotta Warriors + Tang Dynasty Evening

**Morning**
- Visit the **Terracotta Warriors**, about an hour outside Xi’an.
- Go early to avoid peak crowds.

**Afternoon**
- Return to the city.
- Visit the **Shaanxi History Museum** or **Big Wild Goose Pagoda**.

**Evening**
- Watch the fountain/light show near Big Wild Goose Pagoda if operating.
- Optional: Tang Dynasty music and dance performance.

**Food focus**
- Xi’an is one of China’s best food cities. Don’t skip the noodles.

---

## Day 6 — Xi’an → Shanghai: The Bund + French Concession

**Travel**
- Fly Xi’an to Shanghai, or take a high-speed train if you prefer rail.
- Flying is faster; train is more relaxed but takes much longer.

**Afternoon**
- Check in around People’s Square, Nanjing Road, Jing’an, or the Former French Concession.
- Walk the **Former French Concession**: leafy streets, cafés, boutiques.

**Evening**
- Visit **The Bund** for skyline views of Pudong.
- Walk along **Nanjing Road** or take a Huangpu River cruise.

---

## Day 7 — Shanghai: Old City, Yu Garden, Pudong Views

**Morning**
- Visit **Yu Garden** and the surrounding Old City bazaar.
- Try xiaolongbao — soup dumplings.

**Afternoon**
- Choose one:
  - **Shanghai Museum**
  - **M50 Art District**
  - **Tianzifang**
  - **Jing’an Temple**
  - **Pudong towers**: Shanghai Tower / World Financial Center / Oriental Pearl area

**Evening**
- Final dinner in Shanghai.
- If your flight leaves late or the next morning, stay somewhere convenient for your departure airport.

---

# Suggested route

**Fly into Beijing → train to Xi’an → fly/train to Shanghai → fly out of Shanghai**

This avoids backtracking and gives the trip a natural historical-to-modern progression.

---

# Budget estimate, excluding international flights

Per person, roughly:

| Style | Hotels | Food | Transport/Sights | 7-Day Estimate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Budget | hostels/simple hotels | local eats | trains, metro | **$600–900** |
| Mid-range | 3–4 star hotels | mix of local/nice meals | high-speed rail + some taxis | **$1,000–1,700** |
| Comfort | 4–5 star hotels | nicer dining | private transfers/guides | **$2,000+** |

---

# Practical tips

- **Payments:** Set up Alipay or WeChat Pay before you go.
- **Connectivity:** Get an eSIM or international roaming plan. Some common Western apps may not work normally in mainland China.
- **Transport:** Use metro systems in Beijing and Shanghai; they’re efficient and inexpensive.
- **Language:** English is limited outside major tourist sites. Have hotel addresses saved in Chinese.
- **Trains:** Book high-speed train tickets in advance, especially around Chinese holidays.
- **Crowds:** Avoid major Chinese public holidays if possible, especially Golden Week and Lunar New Year.

---

## If you want a slower version

If you dislike changing cities often, do this instead:

**Days 1–4: Beijing**  
Forbidden City, hutongs, Great Wall, Summer Palace, Temple of Heaven

**Days 5–7: Shanghai + Suzhou day trip**  
The Bund, Yu Garden, French Concession, Shanghai Museum, Suzhou canals/gardens

This version is easier logistically and better for families or first-time Asia travelers.
